relevance_note: This review of succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase (SSADH) deficiency reports individual-level clinical data for in-scope patients, for example "an SSADH-deficient patient" treated with taurine and the literature table "Table 1: Outcomes of VGB intervention in SSADH Deficiencya".
method_note: Read the paper, the schema and the rules; no script was used and no other file was opened. All spans were copied from the Markdown by hand and re-checked with a text search. In-scope people: the 2-year old male taurine patient described from Saronwala and colleagues (2008) (label 'patient'); the 9 literature patients of Table 1 (labels 'Table 1 row 1'..'Table 1 row 9', per-patient reference column copied into source_reference_in_review); the 4 patients of Table 2 (labels 'Table 2 #1'..'Table 2 #4', the table has a bare-number Patient column 1-4, per rule v4, and the table notes say '(reprinted from Gibson et al 1995)'). The 16 patients of the open-label taurine trial ('Sixteen patients were recruited and provided baseline data: 6M/10F, age range at enrollment 2-28 yrs (mean 12 yrs)') have no individual-level detail beyond group counts, so they get no rows and are counted in publications.cohort_size_as_stated = 16. Table 1 is a table of patients as rows with no label column, so labels follow rule 3; its 'Age (yrs)' column is the age at VGB intervention, not an age at diagnosis or at last evaluation, so no age field was filled for those patients and this is noted here. Table 1's 'Clinical Improvement' column names the symptoms that improved (e.g. 'ataxia', 'hypotonia', 'EEG (swd)b'); only entries that are themselves feature names were taken as evidence that the feature was present (ataxia, hypotonia, EEG spike wave discharge). Entries 'IQ', 'cognition, behavior (low dose)' and 'communication' were not mapped onto checklist items (intellectual disability, attention problems or ADHD, speech or language impairment) because the paper does not name those features; likewise 'hyperactivity' and 'agitation behavior' were not mapped onto 'attention problems or ADHD' or 'aggression or disruptive behavior'. 'none' in Table 1 row 1 is a treatment outcome, not an absence of clinical features, so it produced no excluded row. Table 2 has no cell containing stacked values separated by ' / '; the Patient column holds the bare numbers 1-4 and each row is one patient, so no D-31 issue arises. Group statements without names were not used for any person: '8 of 23 patients taking VGB had new-onset, reversible MRI T(2)-weighted hyperintensities and restricted diffusion in thalami, globus pallidus, dentate nuclei, brainstem, or corpus callosum (Pearl et al 2009b)' and 'Four patients treated with VGB (40-100 mg/kg/d) for 1-12 months underwent lumbar puncture ... there were variable improvements in cerebellar signs, concentration, hyperactivity, agility and cognitive function'. The paper prints no ALDH5A1 variant description and ties no variant to any person (it only names the gene: 'SSADH, or ALDH5A1 (aldehyde dehydrogenase 5a1)'), so the variants table is empty and no zygosity, inheritance or pathogenicity could be recorded. publications.n_patients_reported is null because the authors state no number of patients with a printed ALDH5A1 variant; the only stated study total is 16 taurine-trial patients. Paper-internal inconsistency worth noting (not a per-person contradiction): the text calls T1-weighted globus pallidus hyperintensity 'a consistent finding in patients' ('hyperintensity on the T1-weighted MRI images in the globus pallidi bilaterally') while other sentences describe T2-weighted hyperintensities and restricted diffusion in the same region. No contradictions about an individual were found.
